articles.title: Bohol marks 13th year after devastating magnitude 7.2 earthquake
articles.description: TAGBILARAN CITY, Bohol — Boholanos on Thursday (October 15) remembered the victims of the devastating magnitude 7.2 earthquake that struck the province 13 years ago. The powerful tremor claimed lives, destroyed homes and churches, and displaced hundreds of thousands of residents. At 8:12 a.m., the exact time the earthquake struck on October 15, 2013, survivors and residents observed a moment of silence, in memory of those who perished in the disaster. Then, church bells rang while sirens sounded for 33 seconds as part of the commemoration. The Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP) and disaster risk reduction management offices in the province […]... articles.title: ‘We expect war to reach the city soon’: Yemenis stockpile as Houthis advance on Taiz
articles.description: Speed of the advance has left people rushing to buy food as basic supplies to the city are cut off by the fighting Ali Abdulsamed spent all day waiting and walking. Like many people in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz, he was searching for some food for his family of six. But each time he reached the end of the queue at the grocers, he was greeted with empty shelves. He would go on foot to the next shop, unable to afford the price of petrol, which more than doubled last week. After visiting more than a dozen stores, Abdulsamed managed to find a 25kg bag of wheat flour – sold at more than twice its usual price. It would have to do, he was lucky to find anything at all. articles.title: Why is Shell being sued over climate disasters in Brazil, Philippines?
articles.description: WASHINGTON, United States — A typhoon in the Philippines and flooding in Brazil. It meets all the criteria,” Thales Miola, a lawyer for the Brazilian NGO Instituto Preservar, told AFP. On Friday, the organization and federal prosecutors jointly filed a lawsuit against Shell’s subsidiary in South America’s largest country.
